brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: 4 base pieces: three full (piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) plus a half-n (piece:0,1,0;half-n), bolted as one group, capped on open faces, lockJoints applied

Three removable full-depth 3-compartment bins that drop in and lift out on their rim: bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3, bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (9 compartments total), staged with M3 screw/nut/standoff heaps
drawer:0#0,1#cut on the cut face of the half-n base at 0,1,0
handle:0,0,0;top mounted on the top cover (cover:0,0,0;full;top) of the centre cell
Single-storey 4-cell footprint with central handle, joint bolts locking the bases, open faces capped; configurator checks fit only, so load/strength in a printed material is not verified

finish.summary: A compact portable electronics organizer: a 4-cell hex base (three full cells in a row plus a half-n cell) locked with joint bolts and capped on open faces. Three removable full-depth div3 bins (9 compartments) are filled with M3 screws, nuts and standoffs; a drawer sits on the cut face of the half-n cell; a carry handle is mounted on the centre cell's top cover. Check_build passes with meshClash clear.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
